title: Tensor with a flat constructible étale sheaf preserves bounded constructibility
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. On the small étale site use the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_X$ and its module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $L$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] which is flat, meaning that $-\otimes_{\Lambda_X}L$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Regard $L$ as $L[0]$ in the unbounded derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and let $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For the ordinary étale derived tensor product [def-kun-derived-tensor], there are natural isomorphisms
$$\mathcal H^i(K\otimes^L_\Lambda L[0])\cong\mathcal H^i(K)\otimes_{\Lambda_X}L\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z).$$
These cohomology sheaves are constructible. Consequently $K\otimes^L_\Lambda L[0]\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, and every cohomological interval $[a,b]$ containing the cohomology of $K$ also contains the cohomology of this tensor product. No finite Tor amplitude is required of $K$.

source.place: Tag 095I, lemma-tensor-product-constructible, and Tag 0961, lemma-tensor-c; flat degree-zero specialization, with the cohomology computation recorded in report.md

proof.text: Put $R=\Lambda_X$ and $F(M)=M\otimes_R L$. By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $F$ is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to this functor on the abelian category of $R$-module sheaves. For every cochain complex $C$ this gives canonical isomorphisms $H^i(F(C))\cong H^i(C)\otimes_R L$, natural in $C$. The total complex $C\otimes_R L[0]$ is exactly $F(C)$: the only nonzero summand in degree $n$ has bidegree $(n,0)$ and its differential is $d_C\otimes1$, by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. In particular this tensor is acyclic whenever $C$ is acyclic. Thus $L[0]$ is K-flat in the sense of [def-pc-kflat-complex], and has flat terms (the other terms are zero).

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, applied degreewise; sites-cohomology.tex, definition-K-flat

proof.text:
Represent $K$ by $C$, and choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to C$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor] is represented by $P\otimes_R L[0]$. Step 1 and the quasi-isomorphism give
$$\mathcal H^i(K\otimes^L_\Lambda L[0])\cong H^i(P\otimes_R L[0])\cong H^i(P)\otimes_R L\cong\mathcal H^i(K)\otimes_R L.$$
Here cohomology of a localized complex is the cohomology of that complex by [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. These identifications are natural on flat-term K-flat models: [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] supplies the natural tensor comparison and the equivalence between their localization and the derived category; the cohomology comparison is natural by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Consequently the displayed comparison descends to the derived category and is natural in $K$. For a map $L\to L'$ between flat sheaves, the maps $C^n\otimes_R L\to C^n\otimes_R L'$ commute with the differentials and carry cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries. The comparisons induced on their cycle quotients therefore commute with this map as well, proving naturality in the flat factor.

source.place: Tags 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, and 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding construction; natural localization comparison as in lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent

proof.text: Fix $i$ and put $A=\mathcal H^i(K)$. Choose the finite constructible locally closed scheme stratifications for $A$ and $L$ supplied by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection] to them. It supplies a finite constructible stratification with strata $V_{k,l}=Z_k\times_XW_l$ and maps to both original strata. Pullback of a locally constant sheaf is locally constant by [lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant], and pullback of a finite sheaf is finite by [lemma-constructible-pullback-finite]. Hence both restrictions to every $V_{k,l}$ remain finite locally constant. For their module structures we use [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]: constant coefficient rings pull back to the same constant coefficient ring, and module pullback agrees with inverse image. Thus the pulled-back local trivializations are trivializations as $\Lambda$-modules.

source.place: Tag 095I, lemma-tensor-product-constructible, common-refinement argument; the global finite-stratification form uses actual fibre-product strata

proof.text: For each stratum immersion $v:V_{k,l}\to X$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] applied to the induced morphism of small etale topoi gives $v^*(A\otimes_R L)\cong v^*A\otimes_{\Lambda_{V_{k,l}}}v^*L$. Its constant ring comparison and its identification of $v^*$ with inverse image are supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The two factors are finite locally constant by step 3. Their tensor is locally constant by [lem-weil-pbc-flc-tensor-locally-constant-part] and finite by [lem-weil-pbc-flc-tensor-finite-part]. The same finite constructible stratification therefore witnesses that $A\otimes_R L$ is constructible by [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Step 2 now proves constructibility of every cohomology sheaf of the derived tensor.

source.place: Tag 095I, lemma-tensor-product-constructible; Tag 095D, lemma-tensor-product-locally-constant; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback

proof.text: If $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$, step 2 identifies the tensor cohomology with $0\otimes_R L=0$ (the exact functor of step 1 preserves zero). In particular, for any interval $[a,b]$ outside which the cohomology of $K$ vanishes, the tensor cohomology vanishes outside that same interval. Together with step 4 this is precisely membership in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The only flatness hypothesis used was flatness of $L$ in step 1; nothing imposed finite Tor amplitude on $K$.

source.place: Tag 0961, lemma-tensor-c, specialized to a flat degree-zero second factor; unchanged bounds follow from the explicit cohomology comparison

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q39-581b47b98 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read in full the item, its 5 steps, the statement of every cited node, the parent thm-fd-transform-well-defined (step 3 uses exactly this item's conclusion) and the unit sk-prop-well-defined. I checked the sources at the cited places: Stacks 095I (etale-cohomology.tex l.11991), 0961 (l.13688), 095D, and Homology 010N (homology.tex l.1545). The statement is unchanged and correct. Small cases: X empty, Lambda=0, L=0 and K=0 give zero. On a point with Lambda=Z/4, L=Lambda flat and K=Z/2[0] (infinite Tor amplitude), the tensor is Z/2[0] with the same bounds. With the non-flat L=Z/2, H^-1=Tor_1 is nonzero, so flatness is essential and the statement is sharp. Step 1: the exact-functor Mathlib leaf plus def-kun's total complex give C⊗L[0]=F(C) exactly (the sign term vanishes), so L[0] is K-flat in the def-pc-kflat-complex order and has flat terms. Step 2: the lem-pc-kflat-resolution model P has no bound condition. Naturality comes from the descent lemma, since P and L[0] both lie in P_R; it uses statements, not proofs. Step 3: the intersection node gives actual fibre-product strata Z_k×_X W_l (so the E3 containment trap is avoided). The pullback lemmas cover concrete-valued sheaves, and prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact (1)-(2) makes the trivializations Lambda-linear. The pseudo-functoriality mu^{-1}=pr^{-1}iota^{-1} is implicit but elementary. Step 4: the ringed-topoi tensor comparison applies with c the isomorphism from prop (1); the locally-constant and finite parts are each used once; the same stratification witnesses constructibility. Step 5 is elementary. Route: the off-unit statements are Lean-closed or Mathlib, except three, which are declared as tool_uses. I accept lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor as generic black-box tools. No new nodes and no duplicate found: lem-sfb-dc-tensor-preserves, det-lem-int-tensor-product and lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology have different coefficients or sites. No SGA. No fixes.
